A COMMUNITY-CENTRED VISION FROM KENYA

No one should
feel forgotten.

Hardship can change a person’s circumstances. It should never take away their dignity.

Hope & Dignity is an initiative taking shape in Kisumu, bringing people together around care, inclusion and a fairer chance.

A NOTE BEFORE WE BEGIN

A beginning, not a finished story.

Our concept is written. The work ahead is to listen to communities, confirm the legal structure, build safeguards and plan a realistic first activity. We’re looking for people willing to help us get those foundations right.

Read the plan

THE STORY

A personal reason
to build something
for others.

“With God,
nothing is
impossible.”

This is personal.

Henry knows what it means to grow up with very little. Those experiences are part of why Hope & Dignity exists.

His vision is not that people should be defined by hardship, illness, disability or the circumstances they were born into. It is that they should be listened to, treated with respect and helped to find appropriate support.

“The rose that grew from the concrete, proving nature’s law wrong.”

Henry’s description of his own journey, shared in the concept book.

Henry Ochieng OnyuroFounder & Chief Executive Officer
The society we hope for

A just, inclusive, healthy and compassionate society where every person lives with dignity, enjoys equal opportunities and has hope for a better future.

What we want to do

Restore hope and uphold dignity through awareness, advocacy, education, empowerment, psychosocial support, appropriate referrals and responsible partnerships.

OUR PRIORITIES

Real life is rarely
just one challenge.

Health, family, opportunity and belonging are connected. Our proposed areas of work reflect the way people actually live.

PROPOSED WORK · NOT CURRENT SERVICE AVAILABILITY

Health. Without the stigma.

Clear information about chronic illness, compassionate conversations about mental health, and responsible pathways to qualified care.

A place for every person.

Respect and participation for people with disabilities, safer families, and awareness of the rights that belong to everyone.

Room to learn. Room to grow.

Life skills, age-appropriate education and connections to learning and livelihood opportunities that can help people move forward.

When life is disrupted.

Careful community mobilisation and verified information during emergencies, in coordination with people trained to respond.

Stock photographs illustrate these themes. They are not records of Foundation activities or images of confirmed beneficiaries.

These plans depend on capacity, legal requirements and suitable arrangements. We do not diagnose illness, provide clinical treatment or replace qualified counselling, legal or emergency services.

HOW WE WANT TO WORK

Care means
doing things properly.

Good intentions are a starting point, not a substitute for safe practice. Our concept book sets out an approach built on respect, limits and accountability.

01

Listen before acting.

Consult communities, include people who face barriers, and do not assume we know what they need.

02

Know our limits.

Work with qualified providers when specialist care or advice is needed. Never promise support we cannot deliver.

03

Be clear about resources.

Build sound records, agreed responsibilities and honest reporting into the way the initiative develops.

GET INVOLVED

There is more than
one way to help.

You do not have to arrive with all the answers. A useful skill, thoughtful advice or a willingness to work together is a good place to start.

01

Bring a skill.

Planning, administration, communication, accessibility or professional knowledge. Tell us what you can offer and the time you have.

Offer your time
02

Build a connection.

If you work with a community group, school, health service or another organisation, let’s discuss where our intentions might meet.

Explore a partnership
03

Offer something practical.

Useful support begins with a real, agreed need. Please get in touch before organising supplies, equipment or an in-kind contribution.

Discuss practical support

We do not collect payments on this website. Any proposed contribution should have a verified purpose, agreed arrangements and a clear record of how it will be used.

THE PLAN, IN PLAIN SIGHT

Read the thinking
behind the vision.

Our seven-page concept book explains the purpose, proposed programmes, values and immediate priorities. It is a working proposal—not proof of registration, funding or an existing partnership.

  1. 01
    Get the foundations right.

    Confirm the legal pathway, build a founding team and develop essential governance and safeguarding policies.

  2. 02
    Listen and choose a realistic start.

    Consult communities and qualified providers, then identify a manageable pilot with a clear budget and responsibilities.

  3. 03
    Keep records. Learn. Adjust.

    Record resources and activities honestly, protect personal information and listen to feedback as work develops.

BEFORE YOU GET IN TOUCH

A few fair questions.

If something is still unclear, ask us. Openness is part of the foundation we want to build.

Is the Foundation already registered?

The supplied concept book describes a proposed initiative, not evidence of registration or government approval. Confirming the appropriate legal structure and registration pathway in Kenya is an immediate priority. Please ask Henry for the latest verified status.

Can I access a programme or receive support today?

The areas described here are proposed, not a promise that services are currently available. Activities depend on capacity, community consultation, safeguards and suitable arrangements with qualified providers. For urgent needs, use the independent contacts listed above or seek an appropriate local provider.

Can anyone volunteer?

You can express interest by sharing your skills, availability and what you hope to contribute. This is not a guarantee of placement. Any role should have clear responsibilities, appropriate orientation and relevant safeguarding arrangements before work begins.

How do donations or practical contributions work?

There is no payment checkout and no published bank or M-Pesa collection account on this website. Before offering any support, discuss a verified need, intended use and record-keeping with Henry. Do not send financial credentials or sensitive documents in an initial message.

What happens when I prepare a message?

Your browser opens WhatsApp in the current tab with your message ready to review. Only the message is required. If you add a name, email or topic, those details are included too when supported by the browser. You still choose whether to press Send in WhatsApp. No enquiry database or automatic mailing-list subscription is used.

How can I raise a concern?

Email Henry directly, or choose “Share feedback or a concern” in the contact form. Keep the first message brief and avoid unnecessary sensitive details. The concept book identifies formal complaints handling, safeguarding and privacy procedures as development priorities.
